project_name: Flipkart Sale vs Stock Market (52-Week Low)

scenes.spoken_phrase_recorded: When our Flipkart has a big sale, we suddenly become interested in buying things. Even products we were planning to buy at all.
scenes.aspect_ratio_selection_rule: In 9:16 vertical delivery, use top-stage 50/50 split card with lower presenter anchor. In 16:9 widescreen delivery, use full-screen visual cutaway returning to presenter on 'Why? Because we see a great discount.'
scenes.editing_action: Split-screen / Upper Stage Overlay (9:16) or Full-screen cutaway (16:9)
scenes.text_overlay_capcut:
THE GREAT SALE RUSH
IMPULSE SHOPPING ACTIVATED
scenes.optional_sound_effect: cash_register.mp3 / subtle shopping cart notification chime at 00:01.50
scenes.transition_in: Hard cut or rapid 4-frame whip-whoosh from opening face camera
scenes.transition_out: Cut back to presenter on camera at 00:05.40 on rhetorical question 'Why?'
scenes.reason_for_placement: Instantly establishes relatable retail-shopping impulse. Short, energetic hook cut that immediately anchors viewer recognition before pivoting to stock market.
scenes.presenter_retention_rule: Presenter returns to screen on 'Why? Because we see a great discount' (00:07.52 - 00:11.48) to maintain human connection.

scenes.spoken_phrase_recorded: Imagine a phone with a MRP of 1 lakh... That phone, if it is available at 50,000, we immediately want to know if this is a really good deal or not. We compare the feature, we compare with the other website, we track the price and then we make a decision.
scenes.aspect_ratio_selection_rule: In 9:16 mobile format, use dedicated portrait workstation visual with animated price tags stacked above. In 16:9 widescreen, display full desk workstation with sequential typographic lower thirds.
scenes.editing_action: Upper Stage Product Card with Synchronized Typographic Beats
scenes.text_overlay_capcut:
Beat 1 (00:14.00): MRP ₹1,00,000
Beat 2 (00:15.50): OFFER ₹50,000 (50% OFF)
Beat 3 (00:17.50): COMPARE. TRACK. DECIDE.
scenes.optional_sound_effect: whoosh.wav on each price card beat pop
scenes.transition_in: Micro zoom-in (1.05x) cut on 'That phone, if it is available at 50,000'
scenes.transition_out: Hard cut back to presenter on 'and then we make a decision'
scenes.reason_for_placement: Demonstrates the rigorous scrutiny consumers apply to electronic gadgets (comparing specs, tracking price drops) before making a purchase.
scenes.presenter_retention_rule: Presenter on camera for 'and then we make a decision. But when a good company stock...' (00:21.50 - 00:29.12) to anchor the pivotal contrast.

scenes.spoken_phrase_recorded: But when a good company is stock studying a 52 -week low, do we react the same way? No, not at all. Because we worry what if the price falls for the 10 percentage, for the 20 percentage. Why is the difference?
scenes.aspect_ratio_selection_rule: In 9:16, place dark candlestick monitor visual on upper stage with red warning drop tags. In 16:9, cut to full widescreen trading monitor with intense dark graphite and subtle red reflection.
scenes.editing_action: Dark Atmosphere Cutaway / Market Monitor Overlay
scenes.optional_sound_effect: Low sub-bass drone / tension riser hit at 00:30.50
scenes.transition_in: Sudden hard cut right after presenter's punchy 'No, not at all!' delivery
scenes.transition_out: Hard cut back to presenter on 'Why is the difference?' at 00:34.80
scenes.reason_for_placement: Creates stark tonal and color shift from warm consumer excitement to cold market anxiety. Visualizes the visceral dread of a falling stock chart.
scenes.presenter_retention_rule: MANDATORY PRESENTER ON CAMERA: 'No, not at all.' (Master: 00:29.12 - 00:30.50) must remain 100% on presenter for direct eye contact and vocal punch.

scenes.working_title: Price Versus Intrinsic Value (The Central Metaphor)
scenes.spoken_phrase_recorded: We know the price, but we don't know the value. That is the real gap. A stock trading at 52 -week low isn't automatically a great bargain.
scenes.aspect_ratio_selection_rule: In 16:9 widescreen, full-screen conceptual balance scale cutaway with spotlight. In 9:16 vertical, use dedicated vertical scale composition with clean negative space for bold headline typography.
scenes.editing_action: Hero Conceptual Cutaway with Extended Breathing Room
scenes.text_overlay_capcut:
Hero Reveal: PRICE ≠ VALUE
Secondary: LOW PRICE ≠ BARGAIN
scenes.optional_sound_effect: Subtle bell ding / resonance chime on 'That is the real gap'
scenes.transition_in: Smooth cross-dissolve (8 frames) as presenter delivers 'That is the real gap'
scenes.transition_out: Cut back to presenter on 'We need to understand the business'
scenes.reason_for_placement: Delivers the central intellectual breakthrough of the entire video. Visualizes the philosophical weight between changing ticker price and enduring business worth.
scenes.presenter_retention_rule: MANDATORY PRESENTER ON CAMERA: Presenter delivers 'We know the price, but we don't know the value' (00:44.55 - 00:46.80) directly to camera before visual reveals the scale.

scenes.reason_for_placement: Replaces market fear with disciplined professional methodology. Reassures viewers that risk can be managed through structured fundamental analysis.
scenes.presenter_retention_rule: MANDATORY PRESENTER ON CAMERA: Presenter on camera for 'That's why valuation alone isn't enough' (01:05.25 - 01:07.40) to underscore authority.
